top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye is a single, sharply defined and mature invention: magic-wavelength trapping cancels Doppler, recoil and lattice light shifts while many neutral atoms are interrogated in parallel, taking optical clocks from about 1e-15 to about 1e-18, reproduced independently in Sr, Yb and Hg. It is distinct from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 single-system control prize if the citation stays on the lattice concept. The two-name allocation is a defensible judgment on decisive contribution, and an award is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to Katori, Ye or their groups (my collaborations with L'Huillier, Lund, ETH Zurich, Schuch, Dahlstrom, Argenti and Indelicato concern attosecond photoionisation and highly charged ions)
